content: The personal information you provide will not be linked to anything you say during the interviews. Before the interview begins, you will receive additional details about the process, and we will ask for your verbal informed consent to participate. Participation in this short survey and the in-depth interviews is entirely voluntary. You are not obligated to take part, and you may withdraw at any time without providing an explanation or facing any consequences. Unfortunately, we are unable to offer financial compensation for your participation in the survey or the interviews, but we deeply appreciate your time and support. The World Health Organization (WHO) is preparing to conduct anonymized in-depth interviews with a small number of transgender individuals to inform the development of HIV guidelines for key populations. By completing this survey, you are expressing your interest in being interviewed. However, as we can only interview a limited number of transgender women and men from diverse regions and experiences, completing the survey does not guarantee selection for an interview. The survey is confidential. Any identifying information you provide will be securely stored and accessible only to the WHO interview team. This information will not be shared and will solely be used for selecting interview candidates. Participation in the survey is voluntary, and you are not required to answer any questions you are uncomfortable with. Identifying information will remain confidential and will only be used for candidate selection purposes. The survey includes basic demographic questions such as your name, age, email address, country of residence, primary occupation or income source, gender identity, and level of English proficiency. If your English proficiency is limited, you may indicate a preferred language for the interview. Additional questions include your current gender, sex assigned at birth, sexual orientation, HIV testing history, HIV status, and whether you have undergone any gender-affirming surgeries. The purpose of these questions is to ensure that the interviews reflect the diverse experiences of individuals at risk of or living with HIV. This will help us select participants with varying HIV-related characteristics for the in-depth interviews. You are not required to answer any questions you do not wish to. If you agree to participate in the interviews, you will be asked to provide a contact method (e.g., phone number or Skype) and a convenient date and time for the interview. The interview will last approximately one hour and will be semi-structured, allowing you to freely discuss topics that are important to you. The interview will be voice-recorded, transcribed, and analyzed. You will be assigned an interview ID number to ensure your responses remain anonymous. Direct quotes from the interview may be included in the final report, but no identifying information will be used. There are potential risks associated with participating in the study, as the interview may include personal questions about your sexual activity, drug use, and transitioning experiences. You may feel uncomfortable answering some of these questions, but you are not obligated to respond to any question you do not wish to answer. While there are no direct benefits to you for participating, your input will help WHO better understand the needs of transgender individuals regarding HIV prevention, treatment, and care. This information will contribute to the development of HIV guidelines for key populations. All information you provide will be handled as confidentially as possible. Your interview responses will be linked to an ID number rather than your name, and only the interview team will have access to the file that matches your ID to your name. The recordings and transcripts will be securely stored, and no identifying information will be included in the final report.
